question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X|<3.2)=0.7330,$ find ${\sigma }^{2},$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8869\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ |

${\sigma }^{2}≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<3.2)=P(-3.2<X<3.2).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3.2<X<3.2) & =0.7330 \\ 2P(0<X<3.2) & =0.7330 \\ P(0<X<3.2) & =0.3665 \\ P(X<3.2)-P(X<0) & =0.3665 \\ P(X<3.2)-0.5 & =0.3665 \\ P(X<3.2) & =0.8665 \\ P(X\le 3.2) & =0.8665\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-coring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3.2) & =0.8665 \\ P(Z\le \frac{3.2-0}{\sigma }) & =0.8665 \\ Φ(\frac{3.2}{\sigma }) & =0.8665 \\ \frac{3.2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8665)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.11)=0.8665\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8665)=1.11.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3.2}{\sigma } & =1.11 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3.2}{1.11} \\ \sigma  & ≈2.882\,88.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(2.882\,88)^{2} \\  & ≈8.31\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
